cover_hook: Farmers paint eyes on cows' bums to fool lions
caption_hook: 🐄 Farmers in Zimbabwe paint eyes on their cows' backsides so lions think they're being watched + 3 more wins you missed 👇
question: Painted cow eyes or a mountain geoglyph: which would you rather see?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves weird science
reel_hook: Why these cows have eyes on their bums
first_comment: Bonus: the farmer's first 'victims' were local dogs, which barked in alarm at the new eyes. Hyenas, though, don't seem fooled at all. What would you paint? 🐄

stories.stat_label: of 683 eye-painted cows lost to lions
stories.headline: Painted eyes on cows' bums are keeping lions away
stories.summary: Farmer Edson Mabika used to lose 4 or 5 animals a year. Since painting eyes on his herd's rumps, he's lost just 2. In a Botswana study, lions and leopards killed none of 683 eye-painted cows.
stories.why: Ambush hunters hate being spotted, so fake eyes save both cattle and lions.

stories.headline: A climber spotted a possible Inca geoglyph on Google Earth
stories.summary: Mountaineer Carlos Gobbi saw stone circles and passageways on satellite images, then hiked 3 days to confirm them. Archaeologists will now study whether the site is an Inca ritual complex.
stories.why: It could reveal ceremonies at the southern edge of the Inca Empire.

stories.headline: A new material uses light to make hydrogen from water
stories.summary: Chemists built a crystal called BVR-19 whose sulfur bonds capture light and split water into hydrogen, with no extra precious-metal catalyst. It even forms by itself in water at room temperature.
stories.why: Green hydrogen costs about $5/kg today; designs like this could bring it down.

stories.headline: A forgotten 30-year forest experiment grew giant trees
stories.summary: Revisiting a 1980s trial in mountain ash forest, scientists found thinned plots grew trees 20% thicker and stored as much carbon as untouched forest. Rare Leadbeater's possums lived in every one.
stories.why: It suggests forests can give timber, carbon and wildlife homes at once.

fun_fact: Many butterflies and moths carry eyespots on their wings for the same reason: to startle predators.
